claims.text: Formation of single-phase noble-metal-based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by kinetic competition among atomic diffusion, nucleation, and growth.
Crystal-structure selection is governed by kinetic competition among atomic diffusion, nucleation, and growth.
Composition influences the kinetic competition controlling formation and crystal-structure selection.
Thermal history influences the kinetic competition controlling formation and crystal-structure selection.
Processing conditions influence the kinetic competition controlling formation and crystal-structure selection.
The proposed initial material is a single-phase solid solution containing more than five elements.
Thermal history and processing conditions will be varied in a controlled manner.
The applicable synthesis regime includes rapid heating and cooling.
Atomic diffusion and nucleation are the structural mediators of the intervention.
Optimizing the kinetic competition can produce a single-phase solid solution with controlled crystal structure.
Failure to optimize the kinetic competition can produce phase separation.
Failure to optimize the kinetic competition can produce elemental segregation.
Failure to optimize the kinetic competition can produce uncontrolled particle morphology.
The stated baseline has uncontrolled crystal structure and phase separation.
The compositional scope is restricted to noble-metal-based alloys containing more than five elements.
The processing scope is restricted to rapid-heating and rapid-cooling conditions and variation of thermal history.
A finding that crystal-structure selection is independent of thermal history and processing conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as a single-phase solid solution, whereas the baseline is described as phase-separated with uncontrolled crystal structure. These cannot both unambiguously define the same initial baseline.
